tagline: General AI advances relevant to chemistry and scientific computing.

seo_description: Follow Chemisters The Artificial Intelligence on LinkedIn and Facebook: news and explainers on AI advances relevant to chemistry and science.

definition.lead: Artificial intelligence is the science of building systems that learn from data, recognize patterns, make decisions and generate content.
definition.body: This page follows the AI advances that matter for chemistry and science: new models, tools and methods, explained for scientists. Breakthroughs from deep learning to large language models often reach chemistry labs within months.

timeline.title: The Turing test
timeline.text: Alan Turing asks whether machines can think, and proposes the imitation game.

timeline.title: Dartmouth
timeline.text: A summer workshop at Dartmouth College launches artificial intelligence as a field.
timeline.why: The name and the research programme are born.

timeline.title: The perceptron
timeline.text: Frank Rosenblatt builds an early learning machine inspired by neurons.

timeline.title: Backpropagation
timeline.text: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams show how to train multi-layer networks.
timeline.why: The learning algorithm of deep learning.

timeline.title: Deep Blue
timeline.text: IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov.

timeline.title: The deep learning breakthrough
timeline.text: AlexNet wins the ImageNet image-recognition competition by a wide margin.
timeline.why: Started the modern deep learning boom.

timeline.title: AlphaGo
timeline.text: DeepMind's AlphaGo defeats Go champion Lee Sedol.
timeline.why: Reinforcement learning mastered a game long thought too hard.

timeline.title: The transformer
timeline.text: Google researchers introduce the transformer architecture.
timeline.why: The basis of today's large language models.

timeline.title: ChatGPT
timeline.text: OpenAI releases ChatGPT to the public.
timeline.why: Brought large language models to hundreds of millions of people.

timeline.title: Nobel Prizes for AI
timeline.text: Physics: Hopfield and Hinton for neural networks. Chemistry: Baker, Hassabis and Jumper for proteins.
timeline.why: AI recognized in two Nobel categories in one year.
